Phase 56 plan: docs/phases/review-bench.md (commit 2711886).

Two parts: (1) round snapshots — every lead submission pins the exact reviewed tree (temp index + git add -A + write-tree/commit-tree, ref under refs/tagteam/snapshots/, row in new round_snapshots table; best effort, never blocks submit). (2) tagteam bench select/run/table — replay a recorded round at claude:<model>:<effort> cells in a detached worktree outside the project, TAGTEAM_READ_ONLY=1, panel verify_verdict contract, usage rows kind=bench with null phase so tagteam report is unaffected; dry-run unless --yes, --max-turns 12 cap, resumable per (round, cell, tree_sha); table = agree / missed-RC / extra-RC / severity counts / tokens / seconds per cell, split by provenance (snapshot exact vs @REV asserted).

Arbiter rulings recorded in the doc: snapshots from now on, historical best effort + labelled; verdict agreement only (no manual labelling until tagteam grade); planted defects follow-up; first run 6x2, 20-round run decided after. Out: codex cells, lens/briefer replay, judging, cockpit view.

Points worth your scrutiny: the future-leak scrub for asserted commits (only the benched cycle's handoff files, phase-doc status not scrubbed); schema v11; capture placement in the CLI submit paths before the on-submit gate.

REQUEST_CHANGES — the scope and verdict-agreement approach are sound, but replay identity and context need these corrections before implementation:

1. Bind snapshots to the reviewed submission version, including AMEND. The plan captures only init/SUBMIT_FOR_REVIEW, yet cycle.py permits AMEND to change the reviewed work in the same round without changing state seq. A verdict after an amendment would currently be compared against the original tree and labelled exact, and the proposed prompt stops at the original submission. Capture/select amendment versions with a distinct entry identity and include their pre-verdict context, or explicitly exclude amended rounds from snapshot provenance until supported. Also describe snapshots as exact submission trees, rather than proof of what a reviewer saw after arbitrary subsequent edits. Test submit -> changed file + AMEND -> verdict.

2. Preserve the implementation diff baseline in the replay contract. A detached worktree at the synthetic snapshot commit has a clean git diff; the saved head_sha is not supplied in the proposed prompt. Give the child an explicit base/tree comparison (or a generated patch) for implementation review, including tracked and untracked submitted changes. Define the baseline for asserted revisions too; do not silently infer that a multi-round closeout commit is a single-round diff. Test that the replay instructions expose the submitted change even though ordinary git diff is empty.

3. Scrub all supported copies of the target cycle's outcome. The listed docs/handoffs JSONL/status/P_T.md paths omit .tagteam/legacy and P_T_cycle.md, both supported by parser.read_cycle_rounds and tracked in this repo. These can directly reveal the held-out verdict, beyond the explicitly accepted phase/roadmap status leakage. Materialize a pre-verdict target-cycle view and remove/truncate alternate copies in both locations. State the remaining Git-history visibility limitation of a shared worktree. Add legacy JSONL and markdown fixtures containing the held-out verdict and later entries.

4. Include provenance in resume identity. The done key (phase, type, round, cell, tree_sha) allows an asserted run at the snapshot commit to suppress a later snapshot run, despite the required separation of those result populations. Include provenance (and the submission version from item 1) in the key and table selection rules. Test identical trees requested once through @REV and once through snapshot selection.

Reviewed the plan against cycle amendment handling, history readers and panel verdict validation. No test run needed for this plan review. The recorded arbiter scope choices (agreement only, labelled historical trees, deferred planted defects, and initial 6x2 budget) remain intact.

Round 2 — docs/phases/review-bench.md @ 25edba3. All four points accepted:

1. AMEND: snapshots are keyed by lead entry ts (submit and AMEND both captured; table submission_snapshots, unique phase/type/round/entry_ts). Reviewed version = last lead entry of round N before the verdict; provenance snapshot only if THAT version has a snapshot; prompt tail runs through it. Snapshots described as exact submission trees. SC2 is the submit → change → AMEND → verdict test (plus missing-AMEND-snapshot → none).
2. Base: snapshot stores base_sha (cycle baseline.sha, else HEAD). Replay is now an isolated git repo built from git archive: commit base, then submitted (parent base) — git diff HEAD~1 exposes tracked + formerly-untracked changes; prompt carries a precomputed --name-status list and says plain git diff is empty. Asserted impl rounds require @BASE..REV (no REV^ inference); plan may give @REV only, base recorded none. SC5.
3. Scrub: pre-verdict JSONL (built from live history) written to docs/handoffs; removed .tagteam/legacy JSONL + both status files, P_T.md, P_T_cycle.md — applied to both trees before committing, so neither files nor replay history hold the outcome. Isolated repo (not git worktree) also removes the shared-history/refs visibility you flagged; remaining stated leak is phase-doc Status / roadmap prose in asserted trees only. SC6 fixtures cover all copies.
4. Resume identity = (phase, type, round, version_ts, provenance, cell, commit_sha, base_sha); table groups within provenance. SC8: same commit via @BASE..REV and via snapshot → two results, two blocks.

Approved. The revised plan at 25edba3 addresses all four round-1 findings: snapshots and replay context follow the last pre-verdict submit/AMEND entry; implementation replay has an explicit baseline and visible change surface; isolated replay history scrubs the supported target-cycle copies; and resume identity distinguishes submission version and provenance. The success criteria cover each correction, including failed AMEND capture and identical commits replayed under different provenance.

The documented limits remain appropriate for this phase: snapshots establish submission-time trees, asserted historical trees may retain outcome hints outside the cycle files, and verdict agreement is not ground truth. The arbiter choices on scope and the initial 6x2 measurement remain intact. Plan-only review; no tests run. Proceed to implementation, with the full suite recorded by the on-submit gate.
